diagnosis.summary: The attempt never reached the stated goal (add node4 to the Galera cluster). Nearly the entire 1200s window was consumed in a repeated kill/restart/retry loop trying to get node2 to rejoin the cluster via rsync-based SST (State Snapshot Transfer), which never completed. The command audit contains no evidence that node4 provisioning or SST to node4 was ever attempted before the executor timed out.

evidence.finding: Rsync SST to node2 repeatedly enters 'joiner' state and stalls: log shows 'Joiner waited 30/60/90/120/150/180 sec, extending systemd startup timeout as SST is not completed' across at least 3 separate restart cycles, each ending in a manual kill -9 of mariadbd/rsync and a fresh retry.

rsyncd log shows the transfer for module rsync_sst completed almost instantly with only 'sent 7652 bytes received 33 bytes total size 283583197' — i.e. only a file list (~7.6KB) was exchanged for a ~283MB dataset, and the resulting datadir on node2 contained only empty schema files (db.opt, orders.frm, orders.ibd) with no confirmation of populated data.

After loading CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY/PUBKEY per platform convention, `ssh node2` and `ssh node3` both returned 'Permission denied (publickey,password,keyboard-interactive)', indicating the SSH pubkey was only appended to node1's own authorized_keys and never distributed to node2/node3.

/etc/hosts on node1 already resolved node1–node4 (10.100.38.10–13), confirming node4 existed and was network-reachable at the OS level, but no subsequent command in the audit targets node4 for MariaDB/Galera setup or SST.

evidence.source: executor command audit, node1 and node2, multiple timestamps (23:32:32, 23:33:49, 23:34:11, 23:42:58)
evidence.finding: Repeated 'Can't connect to local server through socket ... (111)' errors on both node1 and node2 mariadb clients, consistent with mariadbd being mid-restart/crash-looped during the repair attempts rather than a stable running cluster.

One command failed outright with an infrastructure-level error: 'AntriebMCPError: origin web server did not return a complete response within the 120-second Proxy Read Timeout window' during a 180s sleep+check command — the exec framework itself timed out mid-poll, separate from the SST failure.

likely_causes.cause: rsync-based SST between node1 (donor) and node2 (joiner) is not completing the actual data copy — it exchanges only a file listing (~7.6KB) instead of the ~283MB dataset, leaving the joiner stuck indefinitely in 'joiner' state. This is the proximate blocker preventing even the pre-existing 3-node cluster from being healthy, well before node4 could be addressed.

Underlying reason rsync SST stalls after the file list is unconfirmed from the evidence available — plausible candidates are a broken/misconfigured rsyncd module (e.g. permissions, path, or exclude rules causing it to treat the transfer as complete after listing), a firewall/NAT path that allows the initial handshake (port 4444 connects per `nc -zv`) but drops or throttles the bulk data stream, or a donor-side issue where mariadbd was itself unstable/crash-looping and killed the SST mid-transfer.

The executor spent its entire time budget in an undirected repair loop on node2 (repeated kill -9 / rm pid files / restart / wait / observe stall) instead of pivoting to a different SST method (e.g. mariabackup) or capturing deeper diagnostics (rsync verbose/debug logs, tcpdump on port 4444) after the first 1–2 stalls. This is a process failure, not a platform failure, and is the direct reason node4 work was never started.

Cluster SSH keys were only installed on node1 and never distributed to node2/node3, meaning any planned use of inter-node SSH (e.g. for copying files/certs, or an alternate SST transport) would also fail. Not confirmed to have caused the SST stall itself, since rsync SST doesn't require SSH, but it left the executor without a working fallback channel.

next_attempt_guidance: Before touching node2/node3 repair, verify the original 3-node cluster is fully healthy (wsrep_cluster_size=3, all in Synced state) on a fresh cluster — do not assume it deployed cleanly; check this first with `SHOW STATUS LIKE 'wsrep_cluster_size'` / `wsrep_local_state_comment` on all three nodes.

When adding node4, if SST via rsync stalls past ~60s with the joiner stuck and rsyncd log showing only a tiny byte count vs. the actual dataset size, stop retrying the same method — capture `tcpdump -i <iface> -nn port 4444` on both donor and joiner during a fresh SST attempt to see whether the bulk data stream actually starts, rather than repeating kill/restart cycles blindly.

Consider switching wsrep_sst_method to mariabackup (if available in the image) as a fallback/comparison if rsync SST continues to stall after one clean retry with verbose logging (`wsrep_debug=1`, `--progress 1`) — but only after confirming via evidence that rsync itself, not something environmental, is the failure point.

Distribute CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY/PUBKEY to every node's authorized_keys (not just the node running the command) at the start of the attempt, since inter-node SSH may be needed for diagnostics or alternate data-transfer paths across all 4 nodes.

Time-box each repair cycle (e.g. 2 restart attempts max, ~5 minutes) before escalating to a different SST method or flagging the blocker — the timed-out attempt spent effectively its whole budget stuck on node2 without ever starting node4 provisioning.

Once the 3-node cluster is confirmed healthy, verify node4 is provisioned with the same MariaDB/Galera image and version as node1–3 before adding it to wsrep_cluster_address, since a version/config mismatch could independently cause a similar SST stall.
